headline: Three charged in AI impersonation scheme accused of stealing about $129 million
body: Prosecutors said Thursday that three people were indicted in New York on wire fraud and aggravated identity theft charges. Prosecutors say they used AI to mimic a CEO's voice and sometimes image on calls, and often targeted companies' accounting departments. Victims included hospital systems in Missouri and California and a bank in Rhode Island, according to court documents.
note: For finance teams, the attack ran through accounting departments and the wire instructions, which suggests payment controls matter as much as the calls and emails.

evidence.text: Three people accused of using artificial intelligence to impersonate corporate executives and attorneys to steal about $129 million have been indicted on charges of wire fraud and aggravated identity theft, prosecutors said Thursday.

Over more than a year and a half, Jacob Soall, 41, Sharon Hazan, 54, and Guy Sheetrit, 42, targeted thousands of companies across the world in their AI scheme, according to the indictment filed in a U.S. District Court in New York.

Their victims included hospital systems in Missouri and California, a bank in Rhode Island, a financial technology company in the United Kingdom, a mutual fund company in Massachusetts and a pet food company in Florida, according to court documents.
They would also coordinate a phone or video call where the defendants used AI to mimic the voice and sometimes the image of the CEO, according to the indictment.
The trio, who have nicknames that include “Rocky Balboa,” “Superman Cash” and “Fat Boy,” often targeted the companies’ accounting departments.
The impersonated attorney would tell the employee to wire large payments to bank accounts across the world, according to court documents.
